caseStudy.summary: Nationwide online bouquet ordering and delivery platform in Ukraine: customer storefront, florist operations panel, admin management, and local payment integrations in an end-to-end marketplace experience.

challenge.title: Connecting the brand with local producers
paragraphs: BuketGo is a flower marketplace operating like a vertical platform: the brand handles demand and payments while local florists produce and deliver. It required Ukraine-specific delivery slots, Same Day flows, and multilingual support.

The customer side needed reliable checkout, order tracking, and ad measurement; florists needed daily stock, order management, and store profiles; operations needed an admin panel and maintenance mode — all in one platform.

approach.title: Multi-role marketplace architecture
paragraphs: We built store, checkout, and delivery scheduling flows in Next.js with florist assignment logic. We integrated local payment providers such as LiqPay, Monobank, and WayForPay without Stripe.

The florist panel covers daily stock selection, Same Day availability, and order statuses; the admin panel covers orders, stock, delivery, and review moderation with separate permission layers. Meta Pixel and CAPI tie ad measurement to checkout and purchase events.

caseStudy.summary: Independent SEO guide and installer-lead platform for Ukraine blackout scenarios: power station, inverter and generator comparisons, city hubs, installer claim flow and a full lead funnel.

challenge.title: Turn blackout search intent into a trusted buying guide
paragraphs: As outages grew in Ukraine, users searched for power stations, inverters and generators. Marketplaces listed products but lacked scenario-based selection and local installer connections.
Zaryadna Stantsiya needed organic visibility and qualified leads for installers — without relying on phone or WhatsApp sales.

approach.title: Mid-tail content plus installer monetization funnel
paragraphs: We built city, product and guide hubs on Next.js App Router, prioritizing UA mid-tail pages with DataForSEO intent data.
Installer claim packages, email automation and a Jettfy portfolio cross-link added trust and the first referring-domain layer.
highlights: UA mid-tail SEO guides and city hubs
Power station / inverter / generator comparison funnel
GA4 + GSC measurement and technical SEO

caseStudy.summary: A comprehensive planning platform for brides and grooms: a web application that brings venue, vendor, and budget management together under one roof.

challenge.title: A fragmented planning process
paragraphs: Wedding planning involves dozens of separate decisions, vendors, and budget items. The Gelinikon team envisioned a platform where couples could manage this complex process in a single digital environment.
Existing solutions were either too generic or focused on only one need. Gelinikon needed a user-friendly, scalable web application tailored to the Turkish market.

approach.title: User-journey-centered development
paragraphs: We mapped couples' planning steps end to end: registration, venue selection, theme discovery, budget tracking, and to-do lists. Each module was designed to be developed independently while remaining integrated with the others.
We aimed for a clean, guided experience in the interface, using step-by-step flows instead of complex forms. On the backend, secure session management and data integrity were prioritized.

caseStudy.summary: An e-commerce platform built from the ground up for a traditional baklava brand rooted in Gaziantep: product catalog, online ordering, shipping integration, and a custom interface reflecting the brand's warm tone.

challenge.title: Missing digital storefront
paragraphs: Gastro Baklava is a brand that has been producing with quality and craftsmanship for years, yet it lacked a platform to tell that story and take orders online. Customers could only order products from the physical store or by phone.

The goal was to bring the brand's warm, trustworthy tone into the digital space, present dozens of product varieties in a clear catalog, simplify the online ordering process with weight and packaging options, and integrate nationwide shipping infrastructure.

approach.title: Brand-focused e-commerce design
paragraphs: During discovery, we mapped the brand's visual identity, product groups (baklava, dolama, şöbiyet, midye, etc.), and customer expectations together. We structured the information architecture around product categories, detail pages, and the checkout flow, then moved on to mobile-first interface design.

During development, we addressed performance, SEO, SSL security, and admin panel needs early on. On product detail pages, nutritional values, ingredient information, and delivery options were presented in a clear hierarchy; we left behind a sustainable structure for campaign periods after launch.

caseStudy.summary: A premium corporate website for an Ankara-based künefe brand: heritage story, flavor catalog, branch information, and a custom interface reflecting the brand's warm, traditional tone.

challenge.title: Bringing brand heritage into the digital space
paragraphs: Özikizler Künefe is a brand that carries years of craftsmanship and Hatay's flavor tradition to Ankara, yet it needed a digital showcase to tell that story and display its range of flavors. Most customers knew the brand from the physical location and had limited information online.

The goal was to bring the brand's warm, trustworthy tone into the digital space, present dozens of künefe varieties in a visually rich catalog, strengthen brand identity through heritage and story pages, and deliver a mobile-first, fast experience.

approach.title: Traditional aesthetics, modern experience
paragraphs: During discovery, we mapped the brand's visual identity, flavor portfolio (Special, Mozaik, Cevizzade, Hasır Kaymaklı, etc.), and target audience expectations together. We structured the information architecture around homepage, heritage story, flavors, branches, and contact flows, then designed a premium interface with dark tones and gold accents.

During development, we addressed performance, SEO, and image optimization early. On flavor pages, product photos, portion information, and descriptions were presented in a clear hierarchy; we strengthened social proof with customer reviews and Instagram integration.

caseStudy.summary: A multilingual corporate website for a Netherlands-based HVAC manufacturer: product catalogs, technical documentation, and a trustworthy digital storefront aimed at the European B2B market.

challenge.title: A scattered product showcase
paragraphs: Treemec manufactures climate control and ventilation units, but its website did not clearly communicate its product range, technical details, and corporate credibility at the same time.

Engineers, installers, and distributors in the European market needed information in different languages. The existing structure was outdated, product categories were scattered, and B2B conversion paths were weak.

approach.title: Architecture from technical content to sales
paragraphs: We reorganized product groups in a hierarchy suited to the HVAC sector: air handling units, heat recovery, kitchen systems, and service pages were connected through clear navigation.

We designed a clean interface reflecting the green corporate identity, highlighting multilingual content, technical documentation areas, and quote/contact flows. We addressed performance and SEO foundations early in the process.

We designed a clean interface reflecting the pink-and-white brand language, optimizing campaign banners, product listings, detail pages, and cart flows with a mobile-first approach.

We built a performance-focused backend architecture for matching algorithms and messaging modules. We brought the mobile browser experience close to native app quality.

challenge.title: Reflecting the salon experience digitally
paragraphs: Santora Kuaför is an established beauty brand serving Izmir with 4 branches since 2010. Its wide range of services — from hair design to manicure, lash lifting, and microblading — needed to be presented clearly and attractively online.
Visitors needed to explore services and reach branches and appointments quickly. The brand's premium salon atmosphere had to be felt in the web interface as well.

approach.title: Visually driven salon showcase
paragraphs: We built a homepage with a dark sidebar and full-screen image grid reflecting the salon's aesthetic language. We gathered services, branches, media, reviews, and blog modules under one navigation, creating a conversion-focused flow with a popular services section.

We added Turkish, English, and German language support. We designed short conversion paths directing visitors to the physical salon through WhatsApp integration, appointment CTAs, and branch contact details.

challenge.title: Showcasing manufacturing strength digitally
paragraphs: Kartek Aydınlatma is an established company producing ceiling fixtures, LED panels, electric meters, and electronic products since 1992. Its broad product range and LUNA and Protokol brands needed to be presented clearly on a single site; the corporate story and production capacity had to be communicated in a trustworthy voice.
Product groups, business partners, blog, and press sections needed to come together under organized navigation; visitors had to reach both technical product details and contact channels quickly.

approach.title: Product-focused corporate showcase
paragraphs: On the homepage, we highlighted ceiling lighting products and the production environment with a full-screen slider. We created separate product groups for ceiling lighting and electric meters; sub-products were listed in a clear hierarchy under each category.

We unified corporate, dealers, blog, and press modules under a consistent menu structure. The contact button remained accessible on every page; responsive design delivered a mobile experience suited to showroom and field use.
highlights: Full-screen hero slider and product showcase

The goal was a modern corporate site reflecting institutional trust, clearly categorizing services, providing easy access to training and blog content, and increasing contact conversions.

paragraphs: We restructured the service portfolio under consulting, training, audit, and document center headings. We designed clear benefit, process, and CTA areas for each service; on the homepage, we highlighted trust building through experience, references, and client testimonials.

We developed a clean interface reflecting the blue-and-white corporate identity, integrating blog, FAQ, and contact forms in an SEO-friendly structure. Mobile-first responsive design and fast page loading delivered a consistent experience across all devices.

caseStudy.summary: A brand site and documentation platform for the cyberpunk-themed Protocol Zero mobile game: entry ritual, lore and game guide, economy modules with Web3 integration — an immersive showcase bringing the Operator experience online.

challenge.title: Turning a lore-rich universe into a clear experience
paragraphs: The Clean Network (TCN) is a mobile game project set in the Protocol Zero universe. Layered content such as the manifesto, Operator identity, squad system, and $TON economy needed to be presented accessibly for both players and the community.
Cyberpunk aesthetics are central to the brand identity; the site had to combine an impressive entry experience with an extensive documentation structure in the same atmosphere.

approach.title: Immersive entry + structured docs
paragraphs: We designed the entry screen and connection ritual with a dark theme and neon accents. On the documentation side, we grouped welcome, getting started, economy, and future modules hierarchically through sidebar navigation.

Critical pages such as The Architect's Message, How to Play, Interface Guide, and Liquidity Pool were supported with rich visuals. Roadmap and official links sections presented community trust and long-term vision under one roof.
highlights: Sidebar docs — lore, game guide, economy

caseStudy.summary: A Web3-integrated web application for an AI-powered match analysis and prediction platform: wallet connection, multi-chain support, real-time analysis showcase, and premium user experience.

challenge.title: Complex data, simple experience
paragraphs: Tsuba.Ai is a platform offering match analysis through AI models processing thousands of data points. However, the technical infrastructure, wallet integration, and payment flows together required a clear user experience.

The target audience includes professional users and the Web3 community; the platform needed to inspire trust while delivering analysis results quickly. Multi-chain support for Chiliz Chain and Solana also had to be integrated into the interface.

approach.title: Data-driven, conversion-focused interface
paragraphs: We designed a premium dashboard with a dark theme and green accents. On the homepage, AI accuracy rate, analysis metrics, and popular matches were presented in a clear hierarchy; the wallet connection flow was highlighted in the right panel.

Web3 payment methods, supported networks, and liquidity pools were grouped visually. Responsive structure delivered a consistent experience on desktop and mobile; performance and SEO foundations were addressed early.
highlights: AI analysis showcase and metric panels
